terms.gloss: contagion, infection: the passing of a disease by contact
evidence: Col. 7.5.6: tum praecipuē ovēs contāgiōne vexentur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Contact, and so the spreading of a disease from one to another; also of a bad example. Contāgium, contāgiī n. is the same word in verse (contāgia, Verg., Ov.).

terms.gloss: festering, a gathering of pus: an infected wound
terms.comment: The medical writers’ word; the verb is suppūrō, suppūrāre, to fester (Cato Agr. 157.3).

phrases.english: to rave as if from some pestilent contagion
Wash the cut with water, so that it doesn’t get infected.

sources: Lewis & Short: contagio · Lewis & Short: suppuratio · Lewis & Short: suppuro
